name: Sekra

anatomy.part: left wing root, where the trailing edge meets the belly
left wrist, on the leading edge
right wrist, on the leading edge

myth: Sekra was the first gull to follow Aun up the cut string, because she wanted to see where the wind went too. She flew so high that frost stiffened her wings, and Tavo the Gale came down laughing and took hold of her tail. He pulled three feathers out for the joke, then let her go. She fell, and the sea was cold, and she was too heavy to climb back. Hesk counted the feathers from the pole and tallied them on her reel. Sekra came home low over the cliffs, and she teaches the young ones to hang on the wind rather than climb it. The Gulls still call her name at dusk. The old women say it is a message: the string is still tied at the north end, if anyone thinks to pull. Mend your net while you wait. Tavo does not care who waits.
verse:
Three grey feathers went
down to the cold sea. Hesk counts
still owed, one by one.
